Bill Ackman Bought Meta "at a Huge Discount." He Says Analysts Are Missing Its Growth ©@Miguel Guasch via Canva, @Omar_Nasif from pixabay via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bill Ackman said on CNBC's Squawk Pod that Pershing Square bought Meta at a huge discount after it announced big capex spending, and that it had bought Microsoft and Amazon the same way when their stocks dropped.

Ackman says analysts put the cost of the AI build-out into their models but give no credit for faster growth, and he sees Muse as Meta's payoff.

Since the end of September 2025, analysts have raised their 2027 revenue estimate for Meta 19% and their 2027 earnings estimate only 1.4%, while consensus has free cash flow negative through 2028.

Meta trades at 18x forward earnings, below its five-year average of 21x, and the next test is its fourth-quarter call in late January.

Bill Ackman says Wall Street's models for Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) are missing something big:

They count every dollar of its AI build-out and give it no credit for faster growth.

On Election Day's episode of CNBC's Squawk Pod, Ackman explained how Pershing Square uses the market's big swings. It bought Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) when investors worried about its capex, and Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) when tariffs were announced. And then:

"When Meta announced big capex spend, we were able to buy Meta at a huge discount."

Asked whether he likes all three spending so heavily, Ackman said yes. They can afford it, he said, and they're seeing strong demand and high returns on what they invest. Then he took aim at the analysts:

"The analysts are kind of factoring into the model the capex associated with the build-out, but not any meaningful change in the growth rate. And I think that's just wrong."

That's a contrarian call: Meta's stock fell 15% in October.

Analysts have growth settling near 20%

Meta's revenue grew 22% in 2025, to $201 billion. Consensus has it jumping 28% this year, then growing about 20% a year in 2027 and 2028:

Meta Platforms (META): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

So once this year is done, the models have Meta growing at about its 2025 pace, with the full cost of the build-out on top.

Analysts have been raising their numbers. Since the end of September 2025, they've lifted their 2027 revenue estimate 19%, and their 2027 earnings estimate just 1.4%. In their models, nearly all the extra sales go to costs.

Meta (META) Stock May Be A Bargain After Huge AI Fundraising
Sasha Jovanovic
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM MST 4 min read
META
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta Platforms has poured large sums into AI infrastructure and raised substantial amounts of fresh capital, while the share price has pulled back from earlier highs. This puts a straightforward question in front of you as an investor: Is the current valuation really supported by what Meta is earning today and what those earnings could reasonably justify over time?

Over the past 3 years the stock has gained 85.8%, which makes it important to ask whether that rise is still grounded in the company's earnings power.

Meta's mix of heavy AI data center spending, bond issuance and large equity offerings can reshape future earnings by affecting interest costs, dilution and the timing of any payoff from those projects.

The analysts covering Meta Platforms have run their own numbers. See what analysts think Meta Platforms's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether Meta's recent earnings, set against this AI spending push and softer share price performance, are enough to justify where the stock trades today.

If you want a quick reference point for how other businesses are being priced around heavy AI and data center spending, scan a curated list of 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Is Meta Platforms a Bargain on Earnings?

The P/E ratio is a clean fit for Meta Platforms because earnings remain the main anchor for how investors value its social and AI businesses. Meta trades at about 20.6x earnings, which is below the 24.7x peer average in large-cap interactive media and big tech, yet far above the broader industry's 9.5x level. That combination indicates the market is still assigning a premium to Meta's profit profile compared with the typical online media group while pricing it more cautiously than some mega cap peers.

Because the Fair Ratio blends Meta's own growth, margins, scale and risk into a tailored benchmark, the current 20.6x P/E is described as undervalued relative to what that model would normally imply for this kind of earnings base. Despite the heavy AI data center push and recent bond and equity issuance raising questions about dilution and cash flow pressure, the multiple is still characterized as trading at a discount to this internally consistent yardstick. Democrats won the House and Senate, and Rep. Frank Pallone, in line to chair House Energy and Commerce, wants to "rein in Big Tech".

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is a Hold at $605.02. Democrats now control both chambers of Congress, which brings tougher regulation on top of a lawsuit bill that has already cut into earnings.

nextheprime / Shutterstock.com

Meta's apps, led by Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, reach 3.64 billion daily active people. The stock has fallen 18.12% in a month. Third-quarter EPS came in at $3.83, missing the $5.70 consensus. The main drag was a $9.89 billion charge tied to a teen mental health settlement with 52 state attorneys general.

Democrats then won both the House and Senate. Rep. Frank Pallone, in line to chair House Energy and Commerce, wants to "rein in Big Tech". Increased antitrust examination also effectively freezes Meta's M&A activity.

Ad Pricing Power at 18x Forward Earnings

Revenue rose 26.1% to $64.60 billion, beating the $63.39 billion consensus. Ad impressions grew 10% and average price per ad climbed 14%. Without the legal charge, EPS would have been $7.40. The stock trades at 18 times forward earnings with a PEG ratio of 0.811.

Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73.0 billion to $76.0 billion. Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, signed up more than 10 million users in a month and a half. Meta expects its AI businesses to start adding revenue in 2027. Reality Labs losses should also narrow to about $15 billion that year.
